verdicts.strongest_argument: I independently reproduced two of the five moves from raw Yahoo daily bars and they are exact: 2025-09-02 close 8.60 -> 2025-09-03 close 7.74 = -10.00%, and 2026-06-02 close 5.62 -> 2026-06-03 close 5.45 = -3.03%. So the factual half is right, and it is also the single most public thing about this company: any participant with a chart has CXM's reaction history, and the only reason the baseline lacks it is a former-name filter bug the baseline itself flags. The conditioning claim, which is the only part that could be information, is factually WRONG rather than merely overfit. The showcase print did not follow a run-up: 20 sessions before 2025-09-02 the stock closed 8.87 (2025-08-04), so the run-in into the -10% print was -3.0%, not positive, and the stock was 4.8% BELOW its own 2025-08-06 high of 9.03 rather than 'near its 52-week high after a run.' Today's setup (+22.6% in 20 days, 7.5% below the 52w high) is therefore the opposite of the 2025-09-03 run-in on the dimension the finding names. Moreover the -10% has an identified idiosyncratic cause disclosed on that call: CFO Manish Saran's departure. n=1, and the one observation points the other way.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Sprinklr beat on Q2 but the stock dropped ~8% pre-market as the CFO disclosed he was leaving on September 19 - the identified cause of the -10% print the finding leans on.
Raw daily closes show 2025-08-04 at 8.87 and 2025-09-02 at 8.60, i.e. a negative 20-day run-in into the print the finding calls 'the same setup as today'.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Baseline history is empty (records bug), so this repairs a pipeline gap rather than a market gap. Tape: 20d run-up +22.6%, -7.46% from 52w high - which is not the 2025-09-03 configuration once you actually pull the bars.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Two or more prior CXM prints entered on a genuinely positive double-digit 20-day run-in that also fell hard, so the conditioning claim had more than one observation and that observation pointed the right way.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Every input is published guidance and the arithmetic is a restatement of it. FY27 non-GAAP OI $139-141m and Q2 $29.5-30.5m are in the 2026-06-03 press release; Q1 actual $31.7m is in the same release; the $144-146m prior guide is in the 2026-03-11 release; the CFO's 'improve gradually in the second half of the year as we expect some efficiency gains' is in the published transcript. The cut was reported and the stock traded on it - CXM closed -3.03% on the print day and then bled from 5.45 to 4.91 by 2026-06-25, and ChartMill's headline that day was literally 'Falls on Soft Guidance Despite Q1 Beat.' Sprinklr also told the street WHY: lower services revenue, incremental AI investment, ViralMoment. And the H2 question is in the wire copy the day before the print: Investing.com's 2026-09-01 preview names 'profitability - management's ability to sustain margin expansion' and 'management's outlook for the second half of fiscal 2027' as two of its three watch items, and puts the 9-analyst mean target at $7.88, i.e. 4% BELOW spot. That is a street that is not positioned for a raise. The only thing not published is the phrase '~30% step-up in the quarterly run-rate', which is division.

prior_publication.what_it_says: FY27 non-GAAP OI guided to $139-141m and Q2 to $29.5-30.5m, with Q1 actual $31.7m, and the OI outlook explicitly attributed to lower services revenue, AI investment and ViralMoment.
The original FY27 non-GAAP operating income guide of $144-146m, from which the June number is a cut.
Day-before preview flags H2 guidance and margin sustainability as the two things investors are watching and puts the mean target at $7.88 versus a $8.21 close.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: No usable chain (413 contracts OI, ATM spread 143% of mid), so I cannot show a skew paying for this. What I can show is a sell-side mean target below spot and a documented -3.03% reaction plus a slide to 4.91 when the same guide was cut in June.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Evidence that consensus H2 OI sits at or above $77m - i.e. that the street is still carrying the FY guide - rather than having already marked it down as the sub-spot price target implies.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The factual base is solid and I checked it: Q2 guide of $214-215m total against $193.5-194.5m subscription does imply ~$20.5m of PS, and the Q3 FY26 precedent is exact ($209-210m/$186-187m implied $23.0m PS versus $219.07m total less $190.3m subscription = $28.8m actual, +25%). So the mechanism is real and the sub-versus-PS decomposition of the beat is genuinely absent from the wire copy - that is why this is not a 90. But three things pull it down hard. First, the street already models the beat: FactSet consensus is $215.6m against a $214.5m guide midpoint, so ~$1m of it is in before you start. Second, the finding omits the counterweight from the same transcript it cites: management guided FY PS to ~$87m, about 10% of revenue and in line with the trailing three-year average, which is an explicit deliberate reset - $87m less $24.7m of Q1 leaves ~$20.8m per remaining quarter, so the 'low' Q2 implied PS is the plan, not an oversight. Third, and decisively for a one-day reaction, the finding does not resolve sign: exactly this pattern (headline beat, poor mix) produced +3.05% in December 2025 and -3.03% in June 2026. A claim that predicts a beat but not the reaction to it is not tradeable.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Reports the Q2 guide of $214-215m explicitly against the FactSet estimate of $215.6m - the street is already above the guide.
Management guides FY professional services revenue to ~$87m, about 10% of total and in line with the trailing three-year average, and Q2 PS gross margin to negative 10%.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: No chain to read. Consensus $215.6m versus guide mid $214.5m says a small beat is already the base case; a 1.5-2.5% beat on the guide lands only 0.6-2.0% above consensus.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Evidence that consensus $215.6m was built off subscription plus $20.5m of PS (i.e. the street took the implied PS guide at face value), which would leave the whole PS overage unmodelled.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The numbers are right - I pulled the disaggregation table and it reads Americas $112,861k versus $117,587k, EMEA $77,045k versus $72,036k, Other $29,573k versus $15,877k - and the observation that Sprinklr's home market is now shrinking while a small bucket carries all the growth is not in any wire copy. But it is published, in an indexed free filing-summary that specifically calls out 'Americas Revenue Decline: $112.9 million, down from $117.6 million,' dated the day the 10-Q was accepted, and twelve sell-side analysts have the segment table. That is the 20-40 band, not the 0-15 band. Two substantive problems with the interpretation rather than the fact. The linkage is loose: the finding says the growth is coming from 'the regions where the Middle East disruption and FX sit,' but the Middle East sits in EMEA, and 'Other' - the +86% bucket - is Asia-Pacific, so the two halves of the sentence describe different segments. And a small bucket nearly doubling (15.9 to 29.6) far more plausibly reflects a lumpy large deal or a reclassification than a genuine 86% regional growth rate, which the finding does not address. Mechanically, geography does not appear in the press release, only in the 10-Q filed days later, so this only surfaces tomorrow morning if an analyst asks.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Auto-generated 10-Q summary explicitly headlines the Americas revenue decline to $112.9m from $117.6m.
The geographic disaggregation table itself: Americas 112,861 / 117,587, EMEA 77,045 / 72,036, Other 29,573 / 15,877.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: No chain. No identifiable move in the tape around 2026-06-04 attributable to geography specifically - the stock fell -3.03% on the 2026-06-03 release, before the 10-Q table existed, and continued to 4.91 by 2026-06-25 on the guidance cut narrative.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Confirmation that the 'Other' jump is organic rather than a single large contract or a reclassification, and that Q2 geography will be disclosed alongside the press release rather than only in the 10-Q.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The quoted language is verbatim accurate - I confirmed it in the filing. But every element of the exposure has been public since 2026-06-04 and, critically, management already SIZED it on the record that day: 'about $3 million to $4 million of slip deals that could have closed in the quarter' plus 'we had to move 54 customers on the fly out of a damaged cloud infrastructure environment in the Middle East to Ireland.' That is in the published transcript, and the 10-Q's UAE data-centre sentence appears in the indexed StockTitan summary of the filing. The 2026 Iran war is one of the most heavily covered stories of the year, so 'the conflict was still live across the quarter' is not a discovery. On magnitude: $3-4m is 1.4-1.9% of a $214.5m quarter, it is what happened LAST quarter, and the company still beat revenue and posted a $31.7m OI. Management characterised the region as having 'a very healthy pipeline' with 'several very large deals over the next 2, 3 quarters.' So a repeat of the same headwind is inside the guide's own experience, not a shock to it.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Management quantifies the Middle East disruption at $3-4m of slipped deals and 54 customers force-migrated to Ireland, while describing the regional pipeline as very healthy.
Filing summary surfaces the 10-Q's disclosure of disruption and possible data inaccessibility tied to a third-party UAE data centre.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: No chain to read a geopolitical-risk skew from. Tape says the market does not treat Iran headlines as CXM events: CXM closed UP at 8.21 on 2026-08-31, the day of the first confirmed Iranian strike on a Gulf state since July.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A quantified Q2 impact materially larger than the $3-4m management already disclosed - e.g. an impairment or a customer-loss charge from the UAE data-centre data loss rather than deal slippage.

verdicts.strongest_argument: I verified the date in the filing itself, verbatim: 'The scheduled termination date is September 1, 2026,' with $125m paid to Citibank on 2026-03-16, an initial delivery of 17,123,288 shares, and $75m of the $200m authorization remaining. So the fact is correct and the finding is right that it is obscure. Three things cap it at the middle of the range. First, it IS published, and not only in the footnote - an indexed filing summary of the same 10-Q states the September 1, 2026 scheduled termination date on 2026-06-04, and the $200m programme with a ~$125m ASR intention was disclosed in the 2026-03-11 8-K and covered as 'starts $200M share repurchase plan.' Second, the same disclosure says Citibank may terminate the ASR EARLY at its discretion, which neither this finding nor its twin mentions - so 'the buying stops today' is not established; it may have stopped weeks ago and there is no filing that would tell us. Third and most important: this is a flow claim, not an earnings claim. By the finding's own arithmetic the dealer's covering is ~$1.09m/day against ~$19m/day of dollar volume, i.e. ~6% of the bid. Removing 6% of one buyer does not set a print-day gap; the release does. A mechanical buyer ending is a fact about the days after tomorrow.

prior_publication.what_it_says: States the ASR has 'a scheduled termination date is September 1, 2026' and notes the financial institution may terminate early.
8-K discloses the $200m repurchase authorization, the intent to enter a ~$125m accelerated share repurchase in the near term, and a programme completion target of March 15, 2027.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: No chain, so no way to see whether anyone is paying for a post-ASR air pocket. Tape refutes the flow-support reading: the ASR was buying continuously from 2026-03-16 while CXM fell from 6.01 (2026-06-01) to 4.91 (2026-06-25), near its 52-week low.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A disclosed final-settlement share delivery large enough to move diluted share count materially, or evidence the dealer's daily covering was a double-digit percentage of ADV rather than ~6%.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This is the same claim as CXM-a#5 off the same filing, and I accept the date. What I reject is the causal attribution, which is the part that would make it information - and I reject it on the tape, not on principle. (a) The ASR has been running since 2026-03-16, so if its covering bid were setting the price it was setting it while CXM fell from 6.01 on 2026-06-01 to 4.91 on 2026-06-25 and made 52-week-low territory. (b) The finding's own sizing sinks it: ~6-7% of a 2.76m-share ADV cannot produce a 54% advance. (c) 'No news gap' is false on the bars I pulled: 2026-08-27 closed 7.94 against 7.47 the prior session, +6.3% in one day, and the whole 20-day advance is concentrated in the second half of August. (d) There is an obvious alternative cause the finding does not consider, and it is enormous: the S&P software index gained roughly 14% in August 2026, its strongest August in data back to 1990, with IGV up over 16%, while CXM's own August was +25.9% (6.52 area on 2026-08-03 to 8.21 on 2026-08-31) - entirely consistent with a high-beta small-cap participating in a sector melt-up. (e) CXM-specific news exists too: the 2026-08-13 appointment of Microsoft's President of Search & AI to the board, covered by Barchart, Globe and Mail, TipRanks, Investing.com and citybiz, effective 2026-08-17, the exact session from which the advance accelerates (6.70 -> 7.40 by 08-21). (f) The 'quoted down 3.3% at $7.94' is overstated: 8.21 to the baseline's 7.9955 is -2.6%, and the intraday print I read was 8.065. Finally, like a#5, the mechanism is flow after the print, not content of the print.

prior_publication.what_it_says: IGV rose over 16% in August 2026 versus SOXX +1% and the S&P 500 +2.5%; a broader software index gained ~14%, its strongest August since 1990 - the beta explanation for CXM's run.
Widely syndicated CXM-specific news two sessions before the advance accelerates - Microsoft's President of Search & AI joining the board effective 2026-08-17.
The September 1, 2026 scheduled termination date, plus the early-termination caveat this finding omits.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Raw Yahoo daily closes I pulled myself: 2026-06-25 4.91, 2026-07-01 5.32, 2026-08-17 6.70, 08-21 7.40, 08-26 7.47, 08-27 7.94 (+6.3%), 08-31 8.21. The ASR spanned the fall to 4.91 as well as the rise, and the rise contains a 6.3% single-session gap.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A daily-volume decomposition showing the ASR dealer was a materially larger share of the tape in August than in June, or a 10b5-1/ASR disclosure of accelerated purchasing in the final weeks.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Every dated element is in published wire copy on its own day and the vacancy is arithmetic from two press releases. Millard's departure effective 2025-11-11 was reported on 2025-11-07 by StreetInsider, TipRanks, Investing.com and MarketScreener; Addis's start on 2026-07-01 was an 8-K plus a press release carried by TradingView, Globe and Mail, Yahoo and StockTitan. The wider fact - that Sprinklr has churned its CFO, its CRO twice and senior sales leadership inside twelve months - is a standard, much-repeated part of the bear case on this name, and the market has already seen what soft guidance from this management does to the stock (-3.03% on 2026-06-03 and a slide to 4.91 within three weeks). I could not verify the Kevin Connolly / NewRocket leg at all, so that piece is unsupported as written. And the sign is not established: a CRO with two months of tenure is at least as likely to set a deliberately beatable Q3 bar as an unachievable one, and the finding's own framing ('the first ever guide set by a revenue chief with two months of tenure') is rhetoric about a fact that has been public since 2026-07-01.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Reports Millard's departure as CRO effective 2025-11-11, roughly seven weeks after his 2025-09-22 start.
Announces Thomas Addis as CRO effective July 1, 2026, reporting to CEO Rory Read - so the vacancy window is public arithmetic.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: No chain. No visible tape reaction to either announcement large enough to isolate; CXM closed 5.32 on 2026-07-01, the day Addis started, in the middle of its post-print trough.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Evidence of Q2 sales-capacity damage - disclosed rep attrition, a bookings or cRPO decline, or a withdrawn segment target - rather than an inference from an org chart.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Dates check out off the URL paths: the Al Jazeera piece is /2026/7/12/ and reports Iranian missiles and drones engaged by UAE, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman and Bahrain, and the 2026-08-31 event is documented as the first confirmed Iranian strike on a Gulf-region state since the July resumption, with a drone engaged by the UAE. So the escalation inside the reported quarter is real. But this is the same 10-Q sentence and the same management sizing as CXM-a#4, and both halves are published: the $3-4m of slipped deals and the 54 customers moved to Ireland are on the 2026-06-04 call, and the Iran war has been front-page globally all year. The exposure framing is also inflated. '44% of FY26 revenue generated outside the Americas' is not Middle East exposure - the Middle East is a sub-slice of EMEA, which management placed 'upper middle' among twelve geographies with good performance despite the headwinds. And the market's own answer is on the tape: CXM closed UP at 8.21 on 2026-08-31, the day hostilities resumed. Against a quarter guided to $214.5m, a repeat of the disclosed $3-4m is 1.4-1.9% of revenue - real, but the same order as last quarter's, which the company absorbed and still beat.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Iran fired missiles and drones at Gulf states including the UAE, whose air defences engaged - globally reported, mid-quarter.
Live coverage of the same war including a UAE 'missile threat' detection - the conflict is continuous front-page news, not an obscure fact.
The $3-4m of slipped deals and 54 customers migrated to Ireland - the sizing this finding presents - was disclosed by management on the record.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: No chain to read a geopolitical skew. CXM rose to 8.21 on 2026-08-31 (from 8.16) on the day of the Gulf strike, and to 7.94 on 08-27 - the run-up ran straight through the escalation, which is the market pricing this at approximately zero for CXM.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A Q2 disclosure of Middle East impact materially above $3-4m, or customer losses / an impairment from the UAE data-centre data loss rather than timing slippage.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This is the highest priced-in item in the brief almost by construction: the source IS the document everybody reported, and the framing it argues for is the framing every outlet already used. On 2026-08-13 Barchart, Globe and Mail ('Sprinklr Adds Microsoft AI Leader to Board of Directors'), TipRanks, Yahoo, Investing.com, citybiz and Simply Wall St all carried it as a board/AI-expertise appointment, and Simply Wall St explicitly read it as deepening board-level AI expertise. No publication I can find claimed a Microsoft commercial relationship, so this finding negates a narrative that was never in the price - which is agreement with the wire, not information. I also could not verify one of its assertions: the 8-K I read contains the related-party and family-relationship language verbatim and the two committee seats, but it says nothing about the Strategy Committee being converted from ad hoc to standing at the 2026 annual meeting; what it does say is that Eileen Schloss was removed from that committee effective 2026-08-17. So that leg is unsupported as written.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Frames the appointment exactly as this finding does - a Microsoft AI leader joining the board - with no claim of a commercial relationship.
The 8-K itself: board expanded 7 to 8 on 2026-08-10, Ribas a Class II director effective 2026-08-17, seated on Nominating & Corporate Governance and Strategy, no arrangement or family relationship.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: CXM closed 6.70 on 2026-08-17 versus roughly 6.52 twenty sessions before 09-01, so the appointment did not gap the stock; the advance to 7.40 by 08-21 and the 6.3% jump on 08-27 sit inside a +16% IGV month. Nothing in the tape indicates a partnership premium to be disappointed.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A published claim - sell-side note or news story - that the Ribas appointment implied a Microsoft commercial or distribution arrangement, which tomorrow's call could then fail to confirm.

interactions: Duplicates. CXM-a#5 and CXM-b#0 are ONE claim off the same 10-Q sentence ('The scheduled termination date is September 1, 2026'); b#0 adds a causal attribution of the July-August advance to ASR flow, which is why it scores higher - the attribution is refutable on the tape while the date is not. CXM-a#4 and CXM-b#2 are ONE claim off the same 10-Q Middle East sentence plus the same 2026-06-04 management sizing; b#2 adds the dated escalations, which are globally front-page. Contradictions inside the brief. a#1 and a#2 rest on the same 2026-06-03 guidance document and point opposite ways at the same print: a#2 says a 1.5-2.5% headline revenue beat is mechanically likely (positive), a#1 says the H2 OI guide is unmeetable (negative). Both can be true and in a one-day reaction they substantially cancel, which is the honest read. a#3 and a#4/b#2 rest on the same 10-Q and sit in tension: a#3 says all growth comes from 'the regions where the Middle East disruption and FX sit' while a#4/b#2 say those regions are impaired - and in fact the +86% bucket is 'Other' (Asia-Pacific), not the EMEA bucket that contains the Middle East. a#0 undercuts b#0: a#0's own showcase print (2025-09-03) was entered on a NEGATIVE 20-day run-in, so the brief simultaneously argues that a big run-in predicts a fall and cites as evidence a fall that had no run-in. Against the baseline. Two structural caveats the caller asked me to state plainly. (1) With 413 contracts of total open interest and an ATM bid-ask at 143% of mid there is NO measurable statement of what this market has priced - no straddle, no skew, no put/call signal. Every 'already priced' number above therefore rests on publication dates and on the tape, not on the market's expressed expectation, and that is a real ceiling on my confidence: it is why I did not push the tape-based verdicts above ~85. (2) The brief does NOT contain the sector-beta finding the task description expected; b#0 asserts the opposite (mechanical ASR flow, 'no news gap'). I tested the beta question myself and it favours beta strongly: the S&P software index gained ~14% in August 2026, its best August since 1990, IGV over +16%, while CXM's August was +25.9% - fully consistent with high-beta participation, and containing a +6.3% single session (08-27) and a CXM-specific board announcement (08-13, effective 08-17). That cuts against BOTH b#0's flow story AND the baseline's inferred 'priced for good news' lean: a run-up that is mostly sector beta is not evidence of positioning into this print, so the baseline's only stated read of what is priced is weaker than it looks, and any finding whose edge depends on 'the market has already bid this up on hope' should be discounted for that reason rather than credited.
